title: The Stefan problem for complete melting of finitely strained solids into viscoelastic fluids
summary: The compressible fluid-solid interaction (FSI) with a thermomechanical phase transition is formulated at large strains within the Eulerian frame. For the deviatoric part, the Jeffreys (also called anti-Zener) rheology with an additional viscosity is adopted. The core philosophy governing the mechanical solid-liquid transition is that the viscous (or viscoplastic) response is temperature-dependent and may fully degenerate to a viscoelastic fluid during thawing, so that there is no elastic response on the shear distortion.
